findings.title: Approved thawing methods used.
findings.comment: Inspector observed beef thawing on the countertop in the kitchen. The PIC was informed and the beef was moved to the sink to thaw under running cold water. Ensure staff are thawing food under refrigeration or running water at all times. Thawing cannot occur on the countertop in ambient temperatures.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.13(B) Thawing. Except as specified in (D) of this section, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD shall be thawed: (B) Completely submerged under running water: (1) At a water temperature of 21°C (70°F) or below, (2) With sufficient water velocity to agitate and float off loose particles in an overflow, and (3) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of READY-TO-EAT FOOD to rise above 5°C (41°F), or (4) For a period of time that does not allow thawed portions of a raw animal FOOD requiring cooking as specified under 3-401.11(A) or (B) to be above 5°C (41°F), for more than 4 hours including: (a) The time the FOOD is exposed to the running water and the time needed for preparation for cooking, or (b) The time it takes under refrigeration to lower the FOOD temperature to 5°C (41°F).

findings.title: Proper cooling time and temperature
findings.comment:
3-501.14: (A) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within in 2 hours from 135F to 70F. Within 6 hours, FOOD shall cool from 135F to 41F or less. (B) TCS FOOD shall be cooled within 4 hours or less if prepared from ingredients at ambient temperature. (C) TCS FOOD received above 45F in compliance with LAWS shall be cooled within 4 hours. (D) Raw EGGS shall be received and immediately placed in EQUIPMENT with air temperature of 45F or less. 
Cheese sauce (2 large pans full) is observed in the walk in cooler at 74F. The cheese sauce was made last night at 7pm according to manager. Cooling temperatures are not documented. At 11:30am the cheese sauce is still 74F. The large pans were stacked on top of each other. The pans were not more than 4 inches deep individually and were covered with pan lids that do not have holes to allow heat to escape. Recommend filling the pans only half full (2 to 3 inches maximum) and cooling items must be separated  and loosely covered so that heat can move away from the food. Use mindful cooling practices. The pans of cheese sauce were discarded.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: 3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. A small pan of cheese sauce is observed in the walk in cooler at 54F it is next to the pans that were put in last night and did not cool. Another large pan of cheese sauce about 1/2 full was on top of the cheese sauce at 74F. The internal temperature of this pan was 58F. One gallon of milk and two flats of eggs were also in the walk in cooler.  Milk and eggs were both 58F.  Pans of cheese sauce and eggs were discarded in the garbage. Milk was poured down the drain.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: 3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). Observed small pan and large pan of cheese sauce half full to be date marked 11.26.22. Today is 10 days in the establishment. The cheese sauce was discarded. This is the same cheese sauce that was out of temperature in the 50 degree range documented in violation #22.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
3-501.15: (A) Cooling shall be accomplished with time and temperature criteria by using following methods: FOOD in shallow pans, Separating FOOD into small portions, using rapid cooling EQUIPMENT, stirring food in container placed in ice bath, containers facilitating heat transfer, adding ice, other effective methods. P (B) When placed in cooling or cold holding EQUIPMENT, FOOD containers shall be: arranged to maximize heat transfer through container walls, loosely covered or uncovered, and during cooling period. C
Pans of cheese sauce cooling in the walk in cooler have tight fitting covers and are stacked so that heat transfer can not readily take place. Use proper cooling practices. Suggest putting less cheese sauce in each pan and leaving uncovered or loosely covered. The foods can also be placed into the walk in freezer for a few hours to knock the temperature down. Stirring regularly during the cooling process is also helpful in rapidly moving the temperature of cooling foods through the temperature danger zone.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. 
As the walk in cooler is used mostly for whole vegetables and cooling can take place in the walk in freezer and  holding can take place in the glass front coolers or prep cooler bottom, the walk in cooler is documented in this section. The unit may have been stuck in a defrost cycle overnight as it is cooling down this morning. Have it evaluated by a professional refrigeration repair service. 
* Do not store food that requires refrigeration for safety in the walk in unit until it can be evaluated and adjusted or repaired.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

The facility is looking for handler training in the Spanish language.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.
The food manager has not accomplished the allergen awareness at this time. Complete the training by next routine inspection.
